name: Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn with Kell Alloimmunization
aliases: Kell Alloimmune Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn
Kell Antigen-Mediated Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn with Kell Alloimmunization

criteria.description: Presence of maternal anti-Kell alloantibodies detected by serologic testing
Evidence of anemia in the newborn confirmed by hemoglobin or hematocrit levels below age-specific reference ranges
Positive direct antiglobulin test (DAT) indicating antibody-coated red blood cells in the neonate
Laboratory evidence of hemolysis including elevated bilirubin and reticulocytosis
Prenatal ultrasound findings suggestive of fetal hydrops or anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of maternal anti-Kell alloantibodies plus evidence of neonatal anemia and a positive direct antiglobulin test
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by laboratory and prenatal imaging findings consistent with hemolysis and anemia.

laboratory: Detection of maternal anti-Kell antibodies by indirect antiglobulin test
Positive direct antiglobulin test (DAT) on neonatal red blood cells
Anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit in the neonate
Elevated serum bilirubin and reticulocyte count
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing fetal hydrops, ascites, or pleural effusions
Postnatal chest X-ray may show cardiomegaly in cases of heart failure
genetic: Kell blood group antigen genotyping to confirm antigen status of mother and fetus
other: Maternal obstetric history of prior pregnancies affected by hemolytic disease
Response to intrauterine transfusions or postnatal exchange transfusions

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of anti-D antibodies instead of anti-Kell
More common and historically predominant cause of HDN
Different serologic profile and antigen specificity
Intrinsic red blood cell membrane defect

redFlags: Severe anemia with hydrops fetalis on prenatal ultrasound
Rapidly rising bilirubin levels risking kernicterus
Failure to respond to standard phototherapy and transfusions
